module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 848

Is the maximum size of a set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never
squarefree (for all $a, b \in A$) achieved by taking those $n \equiv 7 \pmod{25}$?

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/848](https://www.erdosproblems.com/848)
 - [Er92b] Erdős, P. "Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics,
   and geometry." Resenhas do Instituto de Matemático e Estatística da Universidade
   de São Paulo 2.2 (1995): 165-186.
 - [Sa25] Sawhney, M. "Problem 848." (2025)
   https://www.math.columbia.edu/~msawhney/Problem_848.pdf
 - Full formal proof of asymptotic result: https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos848

/-- A set $A$ has the non-squarefree product property if $ab + 1$ is not squarefree
for all $a, b ∈ A$. -/
def NonSquarefreeProductProp (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ¬Squarefree (a * b + 1)

/-- The candidate extremal set: $\{n ∈ \{0, \dots, N-1\} : n ≡ 7 (mod 25)\}$. -/
def A₇ (N : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.range N).filter (fun n => n % 25 = 7)

/-- The Erdős Problem 848 statement for a fixed $N$: any set $A ⊆ \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ with
the non-squarefree product property has cardinality at most $|A₇(N)|$. -/
def Erdos848For (N : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.range N → NonSquarefreeProductProp A →
    A.card ≤ (A₇ N).card

/-- Is the maximum size of a set $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never squarefree
(for all $a, b ∈ A$) achieved by taking those $n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}$?

This asks whether `Erdos848 N` holds for all $N$ (formulated using `A ⊆ Finset.range N`).

This was solved for all sufficiently large $N$ by Sawhney in this note. In fact, Sawhney proves
something slightly stronger, that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that if
$\lvert A\rvert \geq (\frac{1}{25}-c)N$ and $N$ is large then $A$ is contained in either
$\{ n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ or $\{n\equiv 18\pmod{25}\}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_848 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ N, Erdos848For N := by
  sorry

/-- There exists $N₀$ such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ satisfies that $ab + 1$
is never squarefree for all $a, b ∈ A$, then $|A| ≤ |\{n ≤ N : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}|$.

More precisely, Sawhney proves: there exist absolute constants $η > 0$ and $N₀$
such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $|A| ≥ (1/25 - η)N$ then $A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}$ or
$A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 18 \pmod{25}\}$.

A complete formal Lean 4 proof is available at:
https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger/blob/1cc2ac8e9d70516e979733c6ea5c4d2eb652d1f5/formal/lean/Erdos/848.lean"]
theorem erdos_848.variants.asymptotic : ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, Erdos848For N := by
  sorry

end Erdos848

findings.description: The module docstring's reference list gives the tag [Er92b] the bibliographic data of a different Erdős paper: "Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry", Resenhas IME-USP 2 (1995) 165–186. In the erdosproblems.com bibliography that paper is [Er95]. [Er92b] is "Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics", Matematiche (Catania) 47 (1992) 231–240. The problem is stated there on p. 239, which is outside the Resenhas page range 165–186. The mathematics is unaffected, but a reader following the reference is sent to the wrong paper.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/848 cites the problem as "[Er92b,p.239]". Sawhney's note (https://www.math.columbia.edu/~msawhney/Problem_848.pdf) gives as its source of the question: "Paul Erdős, Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics, vol. 47, 1992, Combinatorics 92 (Catania, 1992), pp. 231–240". Other FC files that use the site's tags agree: ErdosProblems/842, 98, 24, 21 and 123 list [Er92b] as the Matematiche 1992 paper, and ErdosProblems/45, 83, 95 list the Resenhas 1995 paper as [Er95]. The journal page is https://lematematiche.dmi.unict.it/index.php/lematematiche/article/view/587 (Vol. 47 No. 2, 1992).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the entry with: "[Er92b] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics*. Matematiche (Catania) 47 (1992), 231–240 (problem on p. 239)."

status_issues.recorded: @[category research solved, AMS 11] with answer(True), i.e. the file records the statement for every N, ∀ N, Erdos848For N, as proved.
status_issues.source_status: erdosproblems.com/848 lists the problem as DECIDABLE, 'Resolved up to a finite check'. Sawhney (Oct 2025) proved the bound only for all sufficiently large N. The range N < N₀ has not been checked: forum posts give N₀ ≈ exp(1420), later claims bring it down to about 2.64·10^17, and a claimed verification up to 10^7 was judged likely incorrect. The problem as Erdős posed it has no 'sufficiently large' restriction, so the ∀ N question is still open.
status_issues.evidence: Site (Wayback snapshot 2026-08-14): 'DECIDABLE — Resolved up to a finite check … This was solved for all sufficiently large N by Sawhney in this note.' Forum, Boris Alexeev, 19 Oct 2025: 'The original problem [Er92b,p.239] has no restriction to "sufficiently large": … Assume next that a_i a_j+1 is never squarefree. This is satisfied if a_i ≡ 7 (mod 25). Is this sequence maximal?' (the site was then updated). Forum, 16 Mar 2026: 'the current best bound is exp(1420)'. teorth/erdosproblems problems.yaml records 848 as 'decidable'. Sawhney, Proposition 1.1: 'There exists an integer N₀ such that if N ≥ N₀ then …'. The file's own formal_proof target says 'Original Problem 848 (STILL OPEN): Is max|A| ≤ |A₇(N)| for ALL N?' and 'The full Erdős conjecture (∀ N) remains open.' The theorem's own docstring also says only 'solved for all sufficiently large N'. FC's precedent for the same situation: ErdosProblems/742.lean (Murty–Simon, 'resolved up to a finite check') is tagged `research open` with answer(sorry). My exact clique computation found no counterexample for any N ≤ 40001, so the statement is not refutable at small N; only the status is wrong.
status_issues.suggested_change: Tag erdos_848 as @[category research open, AMS 11] and replace answer(True) by answer(sorry), leaving the statement unchanged. Keep erdos_848.variants.asymptotic as research solved with its formal_proof.

reformulations.difference: The source asks about A ⊆ {1,…,N} and the class {n ≤ N : n ≡ 7 (mod 25)}, and asks whether the maximum size is achieved by that class. The Lean instead quantifies over A ⊆ Finset.range N = {0,…,N−1}, compares with A₇ N = {n < N : n % 25 = 7}, and states only the upper bound |A| ≤ |A₇ N|. So the Lean N is the source's N−1, and the Lean states a bound rather than 'the maximum equals'. This affects both erdos_848 (∀ N) and erdos_848.variants.asymptotic (∀ᶠ N).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The property forces 0 ∉ A, because a = b = 0 gives 0·0+1 = 1, which is squarefree. Also 0 ∉ A₇. Hence Erdos848For (N+1) ↔ Source(N), and both Erdos848For 0 and Source(0) hold trivially. It follows that (∀ N, Erdos848For N) ↔ (∀ N, Source N) and (∀ᶠ N, Erdos848For N) ↔ (∀ᶠ N, Source N). The class-7 set itself has the property: a ≡ b ≡ 7 (mod 25) gives ab+1 ≡ 50 ≡ 0 (mod 25). So the upper bound is equivalent to 'the maximum equals the size of the class-7 set'. I proved all of this in Lean with only the standard axioms: shift_iff, forall_iff and eventually_iff against SourceFor N := ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, NonSquarefreeProductProp A → A.card ≤ ((Icc 1 N).filter (·%25=7)).card; and source_max_iff : IsGreatest {k | ∃ A ⊆ Icc 1 N, P A ∧ A.card = k} (class-7 count) ↔ SourceFor N.

could_not_verify: Erdős's exact original wording in [Er92b, p. 239]. The Le Matematiche PDF is a scanned image with no text layer, so I relied on the site's statement ('for all a,b ∈ A') and on Boris Alexeev's forum quotation ('Assume next that a_i a_j+1 is never squarefree … Is this sequence maximal?'). The quotation leaves i = j versus i ≠ j implicit. The site and Sawhney both include a = b, as the Lean does.
review.notes:
1) The only substantive problem is the status of erdos_848: it is tagged solved with answer(True) although only the large-N case is proved. I reported this under status_issues, as the instructions require. The statement itself, ∀ N, Erdos848For N, faithfully poses the problem.

2) Computational check. I wrote an exact solver in C. It uses the fact that the classes 7 and 18 (mod 25) are each cliques, computes the best combination of the two by bipartite matching (König), and branch-and-bounds over the remaining vertices. It agrees with a Bron–Kerbosch brute force for all N ≤ 1500 and correctly flags violations when the bound is replaced by the class-18 count. Result: Erdos848For N holds for every N ≤ 40001. In exact mode up to 5000, the maximum clique size equals |A₇(N)| exactly.

3) The formal_proof on erdos_848.variants.asymptotic checks out. I built the linked file under its pinned toolchain (Lean v4.27.0, Mathlib v4.27.0 at rev a3a10db); `Erdos848.problem_848_asymptotic : ∃ N₀, ∀ N ≥ N₀, Problem848Statement N` depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. `Problem848Statement`, `NonSquarefreeProductProp` and `A₇` are verbatim FC's definitions, and ∃ N₀ ∀ N ≥ N₀ is `Filter.eventually_atTop`. Under FC's own v4.33.1 toolchain the file fails with 18 API-drift errors, which is irrelevant to the claim.

4) Two trivial docstring slips in erdos_848: it refers to `Erdos848 N`, which is the namespace (the predicate is `Erdos848For N`), and it says 'in this note' without a link.

5) The inclusion of a = b follows the site and matters for small N. Under a distinct-pairs reading, {19,33,35,46,53} satisfies the condition (verified), giving 5 elements ≤ 53 against 2 in the class-7 set. The Lean correctly follows the site's 'for all a,b ∈ A'.
